title: Garmin Watch Studio
summary: Design a watch face visually, preview its information hierarchy and preserve the design as JSON. Studio 2 provides the editing workspace; the accompanying Monkey C source and build tools translate supported designs into a watch application. A browser preview is not proof that every simulated field or hold interaction is available on the physical watch.
features: Select, show/hide and position time, date, health, battery, weather and custom information.
Compare colour treatments and the separate low-power layout.
Preview configured hold targets and see unavailable interactions explicitly.
Preview dawn, sunrise, sunset, dusk and other sky fields against a chosen time.
Open/save JSON and export an image; Undo and guides help arrange elements.
Generate supported assets, compile live/preview applications and compare simulator captures.
workflows: Open Watch-Face-Studio.html and choose Day. Use a fixed Preview time so changing time does not distract from spacing.
Choose a field in Layers or click it on the canvas. Drag it into position; Control/Command-click selects several and Alt-click selects underneath overlapping elements.
Use Add a field for another data item and Show guides for alignment. Hide unused fields rather than crowding the face.
Check Night and Always-on. Day and Night share positions, while the always-on layout needs its own readability review.
Open Interactions and use Test holds to understand the intended press-and-hold targets. An unavailable Wallet label is a limitation, not a working launcher.
Compare a few preview times and read the solar ribbon. Sample heart rate, weather and sport fixtures are demonstration data.
Check the documented capability matrix before treating any field as live. Fields marked verify API require target-device verification.
Save design as JSON, retain a named version and export an image for visual review. The image cannot reconstruct the editable design.
Use the existing design pipeline only with an explicitly selected design. Keep signing keys and the Garmin SDK outside this repository.
Compile both live and preview builds, capture the Garmin simulator and compare against the editor before installing on a watch.
Test actual readability, interactions and power use on hardware. Browser success alone is insufficient for a release.
limits: Target and API assumptions are recorded in the source README. No new simulator or physical-watch build was run in this documentation update. Public redistribution also needs a review of bundled assets and installation-specific references.
